The Non-goals section (requirements.md:250-257) is explicit and itemized: implementing #139's scan, implementing #140's setting or touching AGENTS.md, changing the pull direction (with the round-2-relevant carve-out that the disclosure must still mention pull-direction transmission per AC-029(e), :254), adding redaction/input_digest/machine-checkable consent objects, removing the egress gate, and rewriting the already-correct half of the loop. Each non-goal states its rationale and boundary rather than leaving scope to inference.

Baseline Constraints BL-001 through BL-009 (requirements.md:280-292) state material constraints explicitly: the egress gate is not removed (BL-001), the manual fallback is behaviour-preserving (BL-002), the non-blocking invariant is preserved (BL-003), protected-file/human-copy handling for lite-spec/SKILL.md and test.yml (BL-004, BL-005), the changelog is not modified (BL-006), the seven DS-006 literals are preserved (BL-007), dual-runtime parity (BL-008), and workflow-state-registry registration (BL-009). Security/approval boundaries are stated concretely, e.g. AC-012 (requirements.md:154-156) constrains the Design-Source record to be an audit trace rather than an enforced authorization, tied to docs/THREAT-MODEL.md:12's NOT-Trusted classification of agent self-reports.

The document's highest-risk claim -- that Design-Source becomes a load-bearing but untrustworthy record (requirements.md:17, INV-011/INV-021) -- has a planned validation surface: AC-012 (:154-156) requires the record be explicitly characterised as an agent-written audit trace, not an enforced authorization, verified by TEST-018 (acceptance-tests.md:119-123). The retention risk is covered by AC-003(c)/TEST-007 (requirements.md:100, acceptance-tests.md:15-17), the authority-assumption risk by AC-029(f)/TEST-050 (requirements.md:112-116, acceptance-tests.md:243), and the pull-direction-egress risk by AC-029(e)/TEST-049 (requirements.md:93, acceptance-tests.md:242).
